experiment_description: Proton-proton collision data at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV were analyzed in the top-quark-pair (t tbar) lepton+jets final state using the CMS measurements of the full spin density matrix of the top quark and antiquark. The spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_ttbar = 1/4(I2⊗I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i⊗I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2⊗sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i⊗sigma_j), where P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The measurement basis was the helicity basis, defined event-by-event in the ttbar center-of-mass frame by the top-quark flight direction k_hat, r_hat=(p_hat-cos(theta) k_hat)/sin(theta), and n_hat=r_hat×k_hat, with the sign convention n_hat->sgn(cos(theta)) n_hat, r_hat->sgn(cos(theta)) r_hat, k_hat unchanged. Events were selected in the phase-space bin 300 <= m(ttbar) < 400 GeV and 0.0 <= |cos(theta)| < 0.4, where theta is the top-quark production angle relative to the proton beam direction in the ttbar center-of-mass frame. Quantum discord of the top quark, the entanglement marker Delta_E, the steering marker T, the Bell-correlation marker B, and mixed-state quantum magic M2_tilde were derived from the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients by minimizing the negative log-likelihood with the CMS covariance matrix while fixing the observable value.
